extracted.intended_audience: patent practitioners, attorneys subject to USPTO Office of Enrollment and Discipline (OED) proceedings
extracted.subtask_description: Standards, procedures, and sanctions applied in a USPTO OED disciplinary settlement/final order regarding attorney misconduct (insufficient-funds checks, failure to timely pay client fees). Covers jurisdiction, disciplinary rules violated, remedial/mitigating actions, and imposed sanctions and reporting/monitoring requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Settlement agreement requirements (37 C.F.R. § 11.25)
rubrics_metrics.description: Settlement agreements submitted to resolve OED proceedings must meet the requirements of 37 C.F.R. § 11.25.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Final Order states the parties 'have submitted a settlement agreement ... that meets the requirements of 37 C.F.R. § 11.25.' If the USPTO Acting Director rejects the proposed settlement, per 37 C.F.R. § 11.26 no reference to the offer of settlement, the contingent acceptance, or the facts stipulated in support of the settlement shall be admissible in evidence in a disciplinary proceeding unless the parties agree in writing to such admissibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Jurisdictional basis for OED proceedings
rubrics_metrics.description: This Tribunal has jurisdiction under 35 U.S.C. §§ 2(b)(2)(D) and 32, and 37 C.F.R. §§ 10.132 and 10.139.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Final Order explicitly cites these statutory and regulatory provisions as the basis for the Office's authority to bring and resolve disciplinary proceedings against registered patent practitioners.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on presenting checks drawn on accounts with insufficient funds (37 C.F.R. § 10.23(b)(4), 10.23(b)(6), 10.23(c)(3), 10.89(c)(6))
rubrics_metrics.description: Presenting the USPTO with checks drawn on a bank account having insufficient funds violates the cited Disciplinary Rules of the USPTO Code of Professional Responsibility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Joint legal conclusions: Respondent acknowledged that by presenting ten checks drawn on an account with insufficient funds he violated these disciplinary rules. The Final Order treats such conduct as professional misconduct warranting discipline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Duty to timely pay client funds to USPTO (37 C.F.R. § 10.77(c))
rubrics_metrics.description: Failing to timely pay fees to the USPTO for which the client provided money violates Rule 10.77(c).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Final Order finds Respondent violated 10.77(c) by failing to pay USPTO fees despite having received client funds for those fees; such failure is a separate basis for discipline beyond presenting NSF checks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dishonored check administrative fee (37 C.F.R. § 1.21(m))
rubrics_metrics.description: A $50 fee under 37 C.F.R. § 1.21(m) is required for processing a dishonored (returned-for-insufficient-funds) check.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Respondent paid the $50 fee for each dishonored check as required; the Order notes specific checks and associated §1.21(m) fees were paid after the fact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consequences of failure to pay issue/publication fees — abandonment under 35 U.S.C. § 155
rubrics_metrics.description: Failure to timely pay issue and publication fees causes abandonment of the application under 35 U.S.C. § 155; Notices of Allowance set a three-month, non-extendable period for payment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Final Order quotes USPTO Notices of Allowance language: the application 'SHALL BE REGARDED AS ABANDONED if the fee were not paid within three months' and that the three-month period 'CANNOT BE EXTENDED.' The Order documents applications that went abandoned for failure to timely pay.

rubrics_metrics.name: Petition to revive for unintentional delay (37 C.F.R. § 1.137(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: An applicant/respondent may file a petition under 37 C.F.R. § 1.137(b) to revive an application for unintentional delay after abandonment due to failure to pay fees.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Respondent filed §1.137(b) petitions (and paid associated fees and costs) to revive applications abandoned for untimely fee payment; the Order records those petitions and payments as part of the remedial steps taken.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provisional application completion requirements (37 C.F.R. §§ 1.53(g), 1.51(c)(1), 1.16(d), 1.16(g))
rubrics_metrics.description: A provisional application lacking the cover sheet or basic filing fee must be corrected within a given time period by paying the basic filing fee and any surcharge to avoid abandonment; the cover sheet is required by §1.51(c)(1) and basic filing fee by §1.16(d).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Order quotes §1.53(g) explaining that applicant will be notified and given a period to pay and file to avoid abandonment. The respondent's handling of a provisional filing and follow-up Replacement Filing Receipt are described in light of these rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Request for continued examination fee and proper filing (37 C.F.R. § 1.17(e))
rubrics_metrics.description: A Request for Continued Examination (RCE) requires payment of the fee under 37 C.F.R. § 1.17(e) and must be filed in the correct application to be effective.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Order documents an instance where the respondent intended to file the RCE and fee in one application but mistakenly filed it in another abandoned application; the mistake contributed to the fee being processed and returned for insufficient funds and is treated as part of the misconduct facts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notices to File Missing Parts — deadlines and extension mechanics
rubrics_metrics.description: Notices to File Missing Parts specify a two-month response period (often extendable by one-month increments with extension fees) and warn that failure to pay basic filing/search/examination fees will result in abandonment or surcharge.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Order references multiple Notices to File Missing Parts that set a 'TWO MONTHS' period (emphasis original), explain extension by one-month increments, and the imposition of a $65 surcharge for filing an incomplete application; Respondent's late responses and payment of surcharges are recorded.

rubrics_metrics.name: Surcharges for filing incomplete applications and late responses
rubrics_metrics.description: A $65 surcharge is required in many instances for filing an incomplete application or for responding late to a Notice to File Missing Parts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Final Order notes Respondent paid $65 surcharges in multiple applications where missing fees or late responses triggered surcharges; payment of these surcharges is considered in mitigation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sanctions available — suspension, stayed suspension, and probation
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED may impose suspension from practice before the USPTO, but the Final Order can stay the suspension and instead impose a probationary period with conditions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Here, Respondent was suspended for two years, fully stayed, and placed on two years' probation. The Order describes conditions under which the stay can be lifted (e.g., failure to comply during probation leading to suspension).

rubrics_metrics.name: Monitoring and reporting conditions for probation — practice management reviews
rubrics_metrics.description: Probation conditions can require the respondent, at his own expense, to hire an approved law office practice management consultant to review the practice and submit compliance reports at specified intervals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Respondent must hire Gisela B. Bradley (or another approved consultant) to review his practice and submit reports at 6, 12, 18, and 24 months addressing compliance with Texas Disciplinary Rules regarding (a) maintaining funds in IOLTA accounts, (b) using fee and engagement letters, and (c) managing trust and operating accounts. If not compliant, the report must identify implicated rules and explain noncompliance. Deadlines can only be extended by written agreement with the OED Director.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication and notice of discipline (37 C.F.R. § 11.59)
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director shall publish the Final Order and a Notice in the Official Gazette and give notice of public discipline and reasons to state disciplinary agencies, courts where the practitioner is admitted, and the public.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Order mandates publication of a Notice of Suspension in the Official Gazette and requires OED to notify disciplinary enforcement agencies and courts per §11.59.

rubrics_metrics.name: Order to Show Cause procedure and immediate suspension request
rubrics_metrics.description: If the OED Director believes the respondent failed to submit timely/complete reports or violated disciplinary rules during probation, the Director shall issue an Order to Show Cause, grant 15 days to respond, and may forward materials to the Acting Director requesting immediate suspension for up to two years.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Order describes the procedural steps: issuance of OSC sent to respondent at last address of record, 15-day response period, and if noncompliance persists the OED Director delivers the OSC, respondent's response, and evidence to the Acting Director and requests suspension. Any review by respondent of such suspension does not stay the immediate suspension.

rubrics_metrics.name: Obligations during suspension and consequences (37 C.F.R. § 11.58)
rubrics_metrics.description: If suspended, the respondent must comply with the requirements in 37 C.F.R. § 11.58 pertaining to suspension (e.g., notification to clients, handling of files/funds).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Final Order states that if Respondent is suspended during probation he shall comply with §11.58 and that the OED Director shall comply with §11.59 when imposing such suspension.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of disciplinary record in future proceedings and as aggravating factor
rubrics_metrics.description: The record of the disciplinary proceeding, including the Final Order, may be considered in future disciplinary complaints or proceedings as an aggravating factor and to rebut any representations by or on behalf of the respondent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Order explicitly provides that the record may be used (1) when addressing further complaints or similar misconduct and/or (2) in any future disciplinary proceeding as an aggravating factor or to rebut statements by respondent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mitigating factors considered in discipline decisions
rubrics_metrics.description: Mitigating considerations include prompt payment of outstanding fees and associated penalties after notice, the limited time period of misconduct, lack of evidence of misappropriation, completion of continuing legal education (including ethics), and adoption of practice management improvements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Final Order details specific mitigators relied upon: respondent paid outstanding fees within 90 days of notice, paid §1.21(m) fees, misconduct occurred within a ~4-month period, no evidence of misappropriation, respondent took 15.50 CLE hours (6.75 ethics), established IOLTA account, implemented bookkeeping and practice-management changes, purchased new software, instituted engagement letters and checklists, and hired a practice-management consultant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement to bear own costs
rubrics_metrics.description: Each party shall bear their own costs incurred to date and in carrying out the settlement agreement and Final Order.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Order provides that the OED Director and Respondent each bear their own costs, and later reiterates that all parties shall bear their own costs.
